title: Co-Precipitation Preparation of Chitosan Biopolymer (x%)-Encapsulated Thiourea/Formaldehyde Composite: Chemical Analysis and Application for the Adsorption of Acid Blue 25 from Water
authors: Masseoud Othmani; Nouha Sebeia; Mahjoub Jabli
abstract: In this work, a series of chitosan (x%)-encapsulated Thiourea/Formaldehyde composites (CS(x%)/TU/FAs) and a reference Thiourea–Formaldehyde (TU/FA) were prepared and systematically characterized. The composites were prepared by varying the mass of chitosan biopolymer (from 0.25 to 0.75 w/v) in order to evaluate how the encapsulation of chitosan can affect the morphology, surface chemistry, crystallinity, and thermal stability. The prepared composites were analytically characterized using SEM, particle size distribution, FT-IR, XRD, and TGA/DTG analyses. The morphology analysis showed that pre-mixing chitosan biopolymer reinforced the thiourea network and promoted the formation of a rougher, more porous surface. The particle size distribution analysis revealed that the incorporation of chitosan in TU/FA affected the TU/FA polycondensation kinetics by promoting nucleation while limiting particle growth. The XRD analysis of TU/FA composite exhibited relatively intense and sharp peaks, indicating a partially crystalline structure. After the incorporation of chitosan in TU/FA, the diffractograms were slightly changed. The main peaks were broadening, chemically shifted, and decreased in intensity, indicating that the chemical modification with chitosan disrupted the internal hydrogen bonding and crystalline arrangement of the resulting composite. The thermal decomposition of TU/FA composite started at 221.2 °C and ended at 586.3 °C. However, the thermal decomposition of CS(0.5%)/TU/FA composite started at 212.9 °C and ended at 599 °C. It is clear that the incorporation of chitosan in TU/FA composite led to a higher thermal stability due to the crosslinking effect and the establishment of more hydrogen bonding. The CS(0.5%)/TU/FA material exhibited the highest adsorption capacity for Acid Blue 25 (110 mg/g), approximately 2.5-fold higher than that of TU/FA (43 mg/g), due to the higher density of amine and hydroxyl groups facilitating electrostatic attraction. The adsorption process was dependent on many experimental factors including pH, time, initial dye concentration, and temperature. Kinetic data followed a pseudo-second-order model, implying a chemisorption process. Langmuir isotherm suggested monolayer adsorption. Thermodynamic analysis indicated an exothermic, non-spontaneous mechanism. Overall, the TU/PAA-5/FA composite combines enhanced structural stability with high adsorption efficiency, highlighting its potential as a promising material for the elimination of anionic dyes from textile effluents.
